questions.question: In John Dryden's 'An Essay of Dramatick Poesie' (1668), which speaker represents Dryden himself and defends English drama and Shakespeare?
questions.explanation: Neander meaning the new man voices Dryden own views praising Shakespeare comprehensive soul and English tragi-comedy.

questions.question: In 'An Essay of Dramatick Poesie', the speaker Crites, who argues for the Ancients and attacks rhymed plays, represents Dryden's brother-in-law:
questions.explanation: Crites represents Sir Robert Howard Eugenius is Lord Buckhurst and Lisideius is Sir Charles Sedley.

questions.question: Which four-line stanza form (decasyllabic lines rhyming abab) did John Dryden use in his 1667 historical poem 'Annus Mirabilis'?
questions.explanation: Dryden adopted the four-line iambic pentameter stanza rhyming abab made famous in Davenant Gondibert.

questions.question: In John Dryden's 1681 political satire 'Absalom and Achitophel', which nobleman is immortalized under the portrait of the fickle 'Zimri'?
options: Anthony Ashley Cooper, Earl of Shaftesbury
questions.explanation: Zimri represents George Villiers 2nd Duke of Buckingham who had mocked Dryden in the 1671 play The Rehearsal.

questions.question: Whom did John Dryden depict under the biblical name 'Corah' in 'Absalom and Achitophel', satirizing his fabrications of the Popish Plot?
questions.explanation: Corah represents Titus Oates the chief fabricator and perjured witness of the anti-Catholic Popish Plot.

questions.question: What is the exact subtitle of John Dryden's 1682 mock-heroic lampoon 'Mac Flecknoe'?
options: A Heroic Poem on the Coronation of Nonsense
A Satyr upon the True-Blew-Protestant Poet, T.S.
A Discourse Concerning the Original and Progress of Satire
An Epistle to the Whigs on Poetic Succession
questions.explanation: The 1682 quarto title page reads Mac Flecknoe or a Satyr upon the True-Blew-Protestant Poet T.S.

questions.question: Which 1687 beast fable in three parts did John Dryden compose to defend his conversion to Roman Catholicism?
questions.explanation: In The Hind and the Panther the milk-white Hind represents the Roman Catholic Church and the spotted Panther the Anglican Church.

questions.question: Which libertarian Restoration courtier and poet authored the bleak philosophical verse satire 'A Satyr against Reason and Mankind' (c. 1674)?
questions.explanation: Rochester A Satyr against Reason and Mankind attacks human pride and rationalism preferring animal instinct.

questions.question: Which 1676 comedy by Sir George Etherege features the quintessential Restoration rake Dorimant, contrasted with an affected Frenchified fop?
options: The Man of Mode, or, Sir Fopling Flutter
questions.explanation: Etherege The Man of Mode centers on the ruthless wit Dorimant and the absurd dandy Sir Fopling Flutter.

questions.question: Which 1677 Restoration comedy by Aphra Behn, set in Spanish Naples during carnival, features the exiled Cavalier rake Willmore?
options: The Rover; or, The Banish'd Cavaliers
questions.explanation: Behn most successful play The Rover follows Hellena and the banished English cavalier Willmore.

questions.question: In Aphra Behn's 'Oroonoko' (1688), which treacherous deputy governor of Surinam orders the brutal whipping and execution of Oroonoko?
questions.explanation: Historical deputy governor William Byam betrays his promise of amnesty and presides over Oroonoko execution.

questions.question: In Act V of Congreve's 'The Way of the World', what decisive legal document does Mirabell produce to foil Fainall's blackmail?
options: A marriage contract witnessed by Foible and Waitwell
A deed of trust signed by Mrs. Fainall before her marriage
A secret codicil to Sir Rowland's last will
A royal pardon signed by King William III
questions.explanation: Mirabell reveals a pre-nuptial deed conveying Arabella Fainall whole estate to him as trustee.

questions.question: Under which fictional astrologer persona, originally invented by Jonathan Swift in 1708 to mock John Partridge, did Richard Steele launch 'The Tatler'?
questions.explanation: Steele adopted Swift popular pseudonym Isaac Bickerstaff Esq Astrologer for The Tatler in April 1709.

questions.question: Within 'The Spectator' Club created by Addison and Steele, which character represents the progressive Whig mercantile and trading interest?
questions.explanation: Sir Andrew Freeport is a wealthy London merchant who voices Whig commercial optimism opposite Sir Roger Tory views.

questions.question: Which satirical literary club, formed in London in 1714, included Jonathan Swift, Alexander Pope, John Gay, John Arbuthnot, and Thomas Parnell?
questions.explanation: The Scriblerus Club met in Arbuthnot rooms at St James Palace to mock pedantry through Martinus Scriblerus.

questions.question: Which member of the Scriblerus Club created the enduring English national figure 'John Bull' in a series of five 1712 political pamphlets?
questions.explanation: Dr John Arbuthnot popularized the honest clothier John Bull in The History of John Bull in 1712.

questions.question: Which 1714 work by Bernard Mandeville, expanded from his 1705 poem 'The Grumbling Hive', argued the provocative thesis 'Private Vices, Publick Benefits'?
options: Characteristics of Men, Manners, Opinions, Times
questions.explanation: Mandeville The Fable of the Bees or Private Vices Publick Benefits argued that self-interest drives economic prosperity.

questions.question: Alexander Pope's 'The Rape of the Lock' was written at the suggestion of John Caryll to reconcile a real quarrel between which two Catholic families?
questions.explanation: Robert Petre 7th Baron Petre had cut a lock of hair from Arabella Fermor causing a rift between the families.

questions.question: From which seventeenth-century French book by the Abbé de Montfaucon de Villars did Pope borrow the Rosicrucian machinery of Sylphs and Gnomes?
options: Entretiens sur la pluralité des mondes
questions.explanation: In the 1714 five-canto expansion Pope drew his elemental spirits from Villars 1670 work Le Comte de Gabalis.

questions.question: In which year's edition of 'The Rape of the Lock' did Pope insert Clarissa's grave speech in Canto V to 'open more clearly the Moral of the Poem'?
questions.explanation: Pope added Clarissa speech modeled on Sarpedon speech in Homer Iliad to his collected Works of 1717.

questions.question: When Alexander Pope revised 'The Dunciad' into four books in 1743, he dethroned the original hero Lewis Theobald and replaced him with:
questions.explanation: In the 1743 four-book Dunciad Pope installed Poet Laureate Colley Cibber as the new King of Dunces.

questions.question: In 'An Epistle to Dr. Arbuthnot' (1735), Alexander Pope delivered a famous satirical portrait of Joseph Addison under which classical name?
questions.explanation: Pope portrays Addison as Atticus who would damn with faint praise and sit attentive to his own applause.

questions.question: Whom did Alexander Pope savagely lampoon as the treacherous courtier 'Sporus' ('that mere white curd of ass's milk') in 'An Epistle to Dr. Arbuthnot'?
questions.explanation: Sporus is a biting attack on John Lord Hervey confidant of Queen Caroline and ally of Lady Mary Wortley Montagu.

questions.question: To which Tory statesman and philosopher did Alexander Pope address his four-epistle philosophical poem 'An Essay on Man' (1733–1734)?
questions.explanation: Pope opens An Essay on Man addressing his friend and mentor Awake my St John leave all meaner things.

questions.question: In Jonathan Swift's 'The Battle of the Books' (1704), which two creatures debate the merits of the Ancients ('sweetness and light') versus the Moderns?
questions.explanation: The Bee gathering nectar from nature represents the Ancients producing sweetness and light while the Spider spins cobwebs from itself.

questions.question: In 1724, Jonathan Swift wrote 'The Drapier's Letters' under the persona of a Dublin draper to defeat whose royal patent for minting copper halfpence?
questions.explanation: Swift pamphlets as M.B. Drapier forced the British government to withdraw William Wood patent for Wood halfpence.

questions.question: In Part III of 'Gulliver's Travels', what is the name of the levitating island inhabited by distracted mathematicians and musical theorists?
questions.explanation: Laputa is the flying island controlled by a giant lodestone whose speculative rulers require flappers to pay attention.

questions.question: What name does Jonathan Swift give to the miserable, decrepit immortals whom Gulliver encounters in the kingdom of Luggnagg in Part III?
questions.explanation: The Struldbruggs are born with a spot on their foreheads signifying eternal life without eternal youth.

questions.question: Which Scottish poet inaugurated descriptive blank-verse nature poetry in the Augustan era with his four-part work 'The Seasons' (1726–1730)?
questions.explanation: James Thomson published Winter in 1726 and completed The Seasons in 1730 reviving blank-verse landscape poetry.

questions.question: Which nine-book blank-verse poem on life, death, and immortality was published by Edward Young between 1742 and 1745?
questions.explanation: Edward Young The Complaint or Night-Thoughts on Life Death and Immortality was a central text of the Graveyard school.

questions.question: In Samuel Richardson's 'Clarissa' (1747–1748), who is the chief male correspondent to whom Robert Lovelace addresses his letters, and who later reforms?
questions.explanation: John Belford is Lovelace libertine friend and confidant who becomes Clarissa protector and executor.

questions.question: Daniel Defoe's 'Robinson Crusoe' (1719) was partly inspired by the real-life four-year marooning of which Scottish sailor on Mas a Tierra island?
questions.explanation: Alexander Selkirk survived alone for four years and four months on an island in the Juan Fernandez archipelago until 1709.

questions.question: Into how many books is Henry Fielding's 'Tom Jones' (1749) symmetrically structured, with each book introduced by a critical essay chapter?
questions.explanation: Tom Jones is divided into eighteen books evenly split into six in the country six on the road and six in London.

questions.question: In Laurence Sterne's 'Tristram Shandy', what is the obsessive 'hobby-horse' of the gentle wounded veteran Uncle Toby?
options: Reconstructing miniature military siege fortifications on his bowling green
Translating the Latin excommunication of Bishop Ernulphus
Compiling an encyclopedia of Christian names and noses
Inventing a philosophical clock to regulate domestic gestation
questions.explanation: Assisted by Corporal Trim Uncle Toby reenacts the siege of Namur and continental campaigns on his bowling green.

questions.question: Which twice-weekly periodical essay series did Samuel Johnson write almost entirely by himself from March 1750 to March 1752?
questions.explanation: Johnson wrote 204 of the 208 issues of The Rambler between 1750 and 1752 establishing his moral prose style.

questions.question: To which nobleman did Samuel Johnson send his famous 1755 letter defining a patron as 'one who looks with unconcern on a man struggling for life in the water'?
questions.explanation: Johnson rebuked Philip Dormer Stanhope 4th Earl of Chesterfield in February 1755 for neglecting his Dictionary until its completion.

questions.question: Samuel Johnson's poems 'London' (1738) and 'The Vanity of Human Wishes' (1749) are formal neoclassical imitations of which Roman satirist?
questions.explanation: London imitates Juvenal Third Satire and The Vanity of Human Wishes imitates Juvenal Tenth Satire.

questions.question: In Samuel Johnson's 'Rasselas' (1759), who is the well-traveled philosopher and poet who guides Prince Rasselas and Nekayah out of the Happy Valley?
questions.explanation: Imlac delivers the famous Chapter 10 discourse on poetry declaring that the poet does not number the streaks of the tulip.

questions.question: In his 'Life of Milton' (1779), which pastoral elegy by Milton did Samuel Johnson famously criticize as having 'nothing of art, for there is nothing new'?
questions.explanation: Johnson attacked the pastoral conventions of Lycidas as easy vulgar and therefore disgusting.

questions.question: Which two Pindaric odes by Thomas Gray formed the very first book printed at Horace Walpole's Strawberry Hill Press in 1757?
options: Hymn to Adversity and The Fatal Sisters
The Progress of Poesy and The Bard
Ode on a Distant Prospect of Eton College and Ode on the Spring
Ode on the Death of a Favourite Cat and Elegy
questions.explanation: Walpole inaugurated his private printing press at Strawberry Hill in August 1757 with Gray Odes.

questions.question: Which mid-eighteenth-century poet authored the celebrated unrhymed 'Ode to Evening' in his 1746 volume 'Odes on Several Descriptive and Allegoric Subjects'?
questions.explanation: William Collins published his Odes in December 1746 dated 1747 featuring Ode to Evening and Ode on the Poetical Character.

questions.question: Which visionary religious poem in free-verse biblical parallelism did Christopher Smart compose while confined for madness between 1759 and 1763?
questions.explanation: Jubilate Agno or Rejoice in the Lamb includes the famous passage celebrating Smart cat Jeoffry.

questions.question: In the 1760s, which Scottish writer sparked a European literary sensation by publishing 'Fingal' and 'Temora' as translations from the Gaelic bard Ossian?
questions.explanation: James Macpherson published Fragments of Ancient Poetry in 1760 and Fingal in 1761 claiming Ossian authorship.

questions.question: Which 1765 three-volume anthology edited by Bishop Thomas Percy played a major role in reviving interest in folk ballads and medieval romance?
options: Specimens of the Early English Poets
questions.explanation: Percy Reliques of Ancient English Poetry published in 1765 deeply influenced the later Romantic ballad revival.

questions.question: Under the persona of which fictitious fifteenth-century Bristol monk did the young poet Thomas Chatterton compose his pseudo-medieval verse?
questions.explanation: Chatterton attributed his antique poems to Thomas Rowley an imaginary fifteenth-century priest of Bristol.

questions.question: Under the persona of Lien Chi Altangi, a philosophical Chinese traveler in London, Oliver Goldsmith published which 1762 epistolary satire?
options: An Inquiry into the Present State of Polite Learning
questions.explanation: Goldsmith Chinese Letters first appeared in The Public Ledger and were collected in 1762 as The Citizen of the World.

questions.question: Which 1778 debut epistolary novel by Frances Burney bears the subtitle 'The History of a Young Lady's Entrance into the World'?
questions.explanation: Fanny Burney published Evelina anonymously in 1778 pioneering the comedy of manners novel later perfected by Jane Austen.

questions.question: Which influential 1757 treatise did Edmund Burke publish contrasting the aesthetic terror of the 'Sublime' with the pleasure of the 'Beautiful'?
options: Reflections on the Revolution in France
A Philosophical Enquiry into the Origin of Our Ideas of the Sublime and Beautiful
Thoughts on the Cause of the Present Discontents
questions.explanation: Burke 1757 treatise grounded the sublime in awe terror and obscurity shaping Gothic and Romantic aesthetics.

questions.question: Which of the following statements concerning Neoclassical literature (1660–1785) is NOT correct?
options: Joseph Addison and Richard Steele founded the daily paper The Spectator in 1711
John Dryden was appointed the first official Poet Laureate of England in 1668
Alexander Pope translated Homer Iliad and Odyssey into heroic couplets
Women were barred by royal decree from acting on the London stage after 1660
questions.explanation: King Charles II royal warrant of 1662 explicitly required female roles to be played by women actresses.

questions.question: Which of the following author-and-work pairings from the Age of Sensibility (1745–1785) is NOT correctly matched?
options: Laurence Sterne — 'The Expedition of Humphry Clinker'
Samuel Johnson — 'The History of Rasselas, Prince of Abissinia'
questions.explanation: The Expedition of Humphry Clinker was written by Tobias Smollett in 1771 whereas Sterne wrote Tristram Shandy.
